intro: Week 8 closed with the Bears burying the defending champion Seahawks on Monday night, four days after trading for Jeffery Simmons. Josh Allen took the Bills' touchdown pass record, the Chargers stayed winless, and the Ravens head into a Thursday night game without a settled quarterback or kicker. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Simmons debuts and the Bears bury the champs, 34-17
top.dek: Jeffery Simmons played four days after Tennessee traded him to Chicago and finished with six tackles and a sack. The Bears beat defending champion Seattle on Monday night to reach 6-2 and win their third straight.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell rests in the hospital after a neck injury
top.dek: Campbell left the field on a backboard on the first play of the fourth quarter in Detroit's win over Minnesota. The team said Monday that early indications are positive. Brian Branch and DJ Wonnum also suffered concussions, so the defense is thin for Miami.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Josh Allen passes Jim Kelly on the Bills' touchdown list
top.dek: Allen now owns the most career touchdown passes in franchise history, counting playoffs. He went 21 of 34 for 289 yards, threw two touchdown passes and ran for another in a 36-10 win over Baltimore.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 324: Tampa Bay's franchise-record rushing total in a 16-0 win
top.dek: Bucky Irving ran for 170 yards and Kenny Gainwell for 140, the first teammates in NFL history with 25 carries and 125 yards each in one game. The old Bucs record was 283 yards, set in 2015.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Ravens host Jaguars Thursday night with the QB spot unsettled
top.dek: Baltimore plays Jacksonville on Thursday, Nov. 5 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Lamar Jackson is headed for thumb surgery, Tyler Huntley is out, and rookie Joe Fagnano is working through a foot and ankle issue. A kicker change may come too.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Allen passes Kelly as Bills roll Baltimore

stories.text: Allen takes the franchise touchdown pass record in a 36-10 rout
stories.summary: Josh Allen passed Jim Kelly for the most career touchdown passes in Bills history, counting playoffs, during a 36-10 win over Baltimore. He finished 21 of 34 for 289 yards with two touchdown passes, a rushing score and one interception. Buffalo pulled away with three touchdown drives on its first four second-half possessions and sits at 6-1.

stories.text: Palmer's hamstring adds to a thin receiver room
stories.summary: Receiver Joshua Palmer left the Baltimore game with a right hamstring injury and did not return. The team has not given a timeline. DJ Moore came back from a two-game shoulder absence and caught a touchdown, and running back James Cook is cleared after a concussion. Right tackle Spencer Brown is also on the watch list heading into Minnesota.

stories.text: Rousseau leads a defense that finally got home
stories.summary: Greg Rousseau had three quarterback hits, two passes defensed and his seventh sack of the season, one short of his career high. Rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun picked off his first pass and has taken the starting job from Maxwell Hairston. Coordinator Jim Leonhard warned that one good week does not mean the unit has arrived.

stories.text: 21: straight field goals for Tyler Bass, a franchise record
stories.summary: Bass hit all three of his field goals against Baltimore, including a 56-yarder. That stretched his franchise-record streak of consecutive makes to 21. Buffalo's defense also held the Ravens to 144 total yards.

stories.text: At Minnesota on Monday night, two 6-1 teams
stories.summary: Buffalo visits the Vikings on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season, 19-15 to Detroit, and quarterback Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury. Watch whether Buffalo cuts down on penalties, since it has drawn 10 or more flags four times this year.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins blow a 13-3 lead to New England

stories.text: A taunting flag flips the game as Miami falls 24-19
stories.summary: Miami led New England 13-3 at halftime, then lost 24-19. Coach Jeff Hafley pointed to a second-half taunting penalty on running back Ollie Gordon that turned a third-and-5 into a third-and-20, and the Patriots scored the next 21 points. Hafley said he likes Gordon's energy but wants him to harness it. The Dolphins are 1-6.

stories.text: Rookie Proctor still in the concussion protocol
stories.summary: First-round guard Kadyn Proctor missed the New England game and remains in the concussion protocol. Hafley said he is progressing through the steps. The practice report Thursday and Friday will show whether he can play Detroit. Jarrett Kingston made his first NFL start in his place and graded well after a shaky opening.

stories.text: Chop Robinson keeps getting to the quarterback
stories.summary: Edge rusher Chop Robinson sacked Drake Maye twice, the third multi-sack game of his career. His second sack ended New England's last drive of the first half. Jordyn Brooks led the defense with 11 tackles.

stories.text: 142: kick return yards for Jaylen Wright on five tries
stories.summary: Wright returned five kickoffs for 142 yards against New England, including a 43-yarder. Hafley called him a bright spot and said the return game improved overall. It was one of few clean positives in the loss.

stories.text: Lions visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Miami hosts Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Lions arrive at 5-2. Miami needs a cleaner second half from quarterback Malik Willis, who threw for 211 yards and two touchdowns but also an interception against New England.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots rally in Miami, 3-0 in the division

stories.text: Patriots erase a 10-point halftime hole in Miami
stories.summary: New England trailed 13-3 at the half and won 24-19 behind three second-half touchdowns from Drake Maye. Mike Vrabel told the team at the break to stay patient and chip away, and the offense did. The win moves the Patriots to 5-3 and 3-0 in the AFC East.

stories.text: Henry and Jacas leave early with a depleted roster
stories.summary: Tight end Hunter Henry left in the second quarter with a foot injury, and rookie linebacker Gabe Jacas hurt his knee and did not return. A.J. Brown was already out, Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins are on injured reserve, and the offensive line keeps shuffling. No update on Henry or Jacas has been posted yet.

stories.text: Maye finishes 16 of 20 with three touchdowns
stories.summary: Drake Maye threw for 199 yards, two touchdowns and ran for another against Miami. He had only 53 passing yards in the first half and then went 7 for 7 for 96 yards in the third quarter. It was his fifth straight game with three touchdowns.

stories.text: 4,000: career rushing yards for Rhamondre Stevenson
stories.summary: Stevenson ran 19 times for 82 yards and became the fourth Patriot to pass 4,000 career rushing yards. He also recovered Miami's late onside kick. The team still has a minus-7 turnover differential, and only Indianapolis is worse.

stories.text: Green Bay comes to Foxborough Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: New England hosts the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch the injury report for Henry and Jacas, and whether Brown returns. The Patriots have turned the ball over in every game this season.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets lose a shootout to the Raiders, 38-33

stories.text: Jets blow a 30-21 lead and lose 38-33 to Las Vegas
stories.summary: New York led 23-14 at the half and 30-21 entering the fourth quarter, then lost on a 53-yard Matt Gay field goal with 27 seconds left. Geno Smith's end zone pass on the final drive was intercepted. The Jets outgained the Raiders 439 to 333 but went 2 for 6 in the red zone. They are 2-6 and have lost three straight.

stories.text: Breece Hall sits again, David Bailey out with a groin
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall was ruled out for the fourth straight game, and Braelon Allen started in his place. Edge rusher David Bailey missed the Raiders game with a groin injury. Coach Aaron Glenn says the team will make sure Hall is fully healthy before he returns.

stories.text: Braelon Allen runs for a career-high 147 yards
stories.summary: Allen carried 21 times for 147 yards and a 21-yard touchdown against Las Vegas. He is the first Jets back since Curtis Martin in 2004 to run for 100 yards in three straight games. Adonai Mitchell added a career-high 142 receiving yards.

stories.text: 95: yards on the kickoff return that flipped the game
stories.summary: Raiders returner Dylan Laube took a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown, the first kick return score by any team this season. It gave Las Vegas a 14-13 lead in the second quarter. The Jets scored on their first six possessions, the first time they have done that since 2008, and still lost.

stories.text: At Kansas City on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: The Jets travel to Arrowhead Stadium to face the Chiefs on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. New York needs to fix its red zone finishing and tighten up special teams. Hall's status will be the main practice report item.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Jackson's thumb leaves Ravens thin at QB

stories.text: Lamar Jackson to have thumb surgery, go on injured reserve
stories.summary: Jackson hurt his right thumb on his first snap back from a three-game ankle absence, and coach Jesse Minter said he will have surgery. The move to injured reserve means at least four missed games, and Minter would not rule out a lost season. Baltimore fell to 4-4 in a 36-10 loss at Buffalo.

stories.text: Fagnano has a chance Thursday, Huntley is out
stories.summary: Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano took treatment on his foot and ankle through the Buffalo game, and Minter says he has a chance to play Thursday. Backup Tyler Huntley has a toe injury and will not play. Kicker Tyler Loop may go on injured reserve, with Jake Moody expected to be elevated from the practice squad.

stories.text: Fagnano makes his NFL debut under fire
stories.summary: Fagnano entered in the second quarter at Buffalo after Jackson and Huntley both went down. He finished 10 of 21 for 91 yards with one interception, and the Bills sacked him repeatedly behind a reshaped offensive line. He may now make his first NFL start on a short week.

stories.text: 4: Tyler Loop's missed field goals this season, all inside 50 yards
stories.summary: Loop missed a 34-yarder with Baltimore trailing only 13-7 at Buffalo, his fourth miss of the year. All four came from under 50 yards. His opening kickoff also sailed out of bounds, and the team now plans to turn to Moody.

stories.text: Thursday night against Jacksonville
stories.summary: Baltimore hosts the Jaguars on Thursday, Nov. 5 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Watch who lines up under center and whether a new kicker steadies the team. The trade deadline is Nov. 10, and another loss could push the Ravens toward selling.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Burrow wins it in overtime, Bengals 5-2

stories.text: Burrow rallies Bengals past Titans 43-36 in overtime
stories.summary: Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns in regulation, then ran in a 9-yard score in overtime to finish the win. Cincinnati trailed by a touchdown entering the fourth quarter and tied it on an 18-yard pass to Tee Higgins with 1:17 left. It is the Bengals' first 5-2 start since 2021.

stories.text: Rookie edge Howell likely headed to IR
stories.summary: Coach Zac Taylor said rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell is likely headed to injured reserve with a wrist injury. Cornerback DJ Turner is day-to-day, so his status for Madrid is open. Neither move is final until the team makes it official.

stories.text: Higgins posts 155 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Tee Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns against Tennessee, including the tying score late in regulation. Ja'Marr Chase added 11 catches for 141 yards and a touchdown. Both topped 100 yards in the same game for the fourth time since 2021.

stories.text: 0-20: Cincinnati's old record when allowing 36 points and committing four turnovers
stories.summary: The Bengals had never won a game in which they gave up 36 points and turned the ball over at least four times. They went 0-20 in those spots before beating the Titans. Burrow threw three interceptions yet still accounted for six touchdowns.

stories.text: Bengals head to Madrid to face Atlanta
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network, at Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid. The Bengals are chasing a fourth straight win. Watch how the team handles the travel and an early kickoff with injuries mounting.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns lose at Pittsburgh again, 27-6

stories.text: Browns drop No. 23 straight in Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Cleveland lost 27-6 at the Steelers and fell out of first place in the AFC North. The Browns have now lost 23 straight regular-season road games to Pittsburgh, tying the NFL record for consecutive road losses to one opponent. Halftime was 20-6, and the Browns scored no touchdown for the first time this season.

stories.text: Watson cleared after concussion check
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson went to the medical tent for a concussion evaluation after a hit from Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker, and Shedeur Sanders played the series. Watson returned and called it standard protocol. He was sacked eight times, and a Cleveland.com columnist warned the pounding puts his season at risk.

stories.text: Fannin posts career-best 154 yards
stories.summary: Rookie tight end Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards at Pittsburgh, both career highs. He leads the team with 35 catches and 411 yards through eight games. Over the last two weeks he has 245 yards on 21 targets.

stories.text: 33: sacks taken by Watson, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Watson has gone down 33 times, including eight against Pittsburgh. That is his second eight-sack game in four weeks and puts him on pace for roughly 70, which would pass the franchise record of 66. Cleveland also allowed eight sacks and managed just 34 rushing yards on Sunday.

stories.text: Browns travel to New Orleans
stories.summary: Cleveland visits the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Saints allow 139.4 rushing yards per game, fourth most in the league, so the Browns want to establish the run early after Sunday's no-show. Pass protection is the other thing to watch.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers take over first place, hit the bye

stories.text: Steelers sack Watson eight times, own the AFC North
stories.summary: Pittsburgh beat Cleveland 27-6 for its fourth straight win and sole possession of first place in the division. The eight sacks were the team's most in a game since 2021, and the Steelers extended their home winning streak over the Browns to 23 games. They now sit at 6-2 heading into the bye.

stories.text: Steelers enter the bye relatively healthy
stories.summary: Insider Mark Kaboly said Pittsburgh is going into the bye in relatively good shape. Receivers Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek could return soon, and defensive lineman Derrick Harmon is expected back. The trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Steelers have been linked to receiver help.

stories.text: Warren runs for 143 yards on 17 carries
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren tied his career high with 143 rushing yards against Cleveland, including a 51-yard run in the first quarter. Rico Dowdle added 56 yards. The Steelers held the Browns to 34 rushing yards in return.

stories.text: 8: sacks on Deshaun Watson, a Steelers high since 2021
stories.summary: T.J. Watt had two, Patrick Queen and Cam Heyward had 1.5 each, and Nick Herbig and Kevin Jobity Jr. added one apiece. Jobity's was the first of his career. Watt now has 20.5 career sacks against Cleveland, the most any player has against the Browns.

stories.text: Bye, then Sunday night at Cincinnati
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is off in Week 9. The Steelers return Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC at the Bengals. The coaching staff plans to use the bye on the red zone offense, where Pittsburgh scores touchdowns on only half its drives.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans exit the bye at 2-5 with fixes to make

stories.text: Texans reach the bye at 2-5 with a long repair list
stories.summary: Houston sits at 2-5 after seven games, and the Houston Press bye-week review points to the same trouble spots. Cornerbacks Kamari Lassiter and Derek Stingley Jr. have no interceptions after combining for eight last season. The offensive line has churned, the run game still sputters, and special teams keep drawing penalties. Houston plays at the Chargers next.

stories.text: Noel is done for the year, Dell is back
stories.summary: Receiver Jaylin Noel went on injured reserve with a toe injury suffered against the Giants, and he is not expected back this season. Tank Dell returned in Week 7 after more than 22 months away and caught a 43-yard pass. Nico Collins, Kayshon Boutte and Marvin Harrison Jr. fill out the group.

stories.text: Stroud keeps producing while the record slips
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud has 1,867 passing yards, which puts him among the top five passers in the league despite the 2-5 record. His best game came in Week 6 against Jacksonville: 312 yards, three touchdowns and a 116.3 passer rating in a 34-31 win. He and the team have agreed to hold extension talks until after the season.

stories.text: 7.5: Will Anderson Jr. leads the NFL in sacks
stories.summary: Anderson has 7.5 sacks through seven weeks, tops in the league. He went without one in Weeks 6 and 7, so the bye gives him a chance to reset. He signed a record-setting extension this year.

stories.text: Texans visit winless Chargers on Sunday
stories.summary: Houston plays at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:05 PM ET on CBS from SoFi Stadium. The Chargers are 0-7 and have gone 27 straight drives without an offensive touchdown. Houston has not posted its Week 9 injury report yet, and its last report before the bye listed four players out.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts stick with Jones after 42-7 loss

stories.text: Colts keep Daniel Jones as starter after 42-7 loss
stories.summary: Shane Steichen said Monday that Daniel Jones will start Sunday against Dallas. Steichen had said after the Jacksonville loss that he would reassess every position. Jones went 19 of 28 for 144 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions before leaving with 11:53 left, and his 39.5 QBR is the second lowest of his career. Anthony Richardson finished the game.

stories.text: No injury detail yet after the Jacksonville loss
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor was out of the game early in the fourth quarter, but no report gives a reason, and no other new Colts injury has surfaced. Linebacker CJ Allen made his first start and led the team with 10 tackles.

stories.text: Taylor still produces while his name hits the market
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor has 610 rushing yards, eighth in the NFL, and 8 touchdowns, second most. He carried 8 times for 23 yards in Jacksonville. He is set to play Dallas unless a trade comes together before the Nov. 10 deadline, and he has said he did not ask to be moved.

stories.text: 2-13: Colts' record since their 8-2 start last year
stories.summary: Indianapolis opened last season 8-2 and has won twice in 15 games since. The Colts are 2-6 this year and have lost four in a row. They have not made the playoffs since 2020.

stories.text: Colts host Cowboys, who cannot stop the run
stories.summary: Indianapolis hosts Dallas on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. The Cowboys allow 152.8 rushing yards a game, the worst mark in the league. The Nov. 10 trade deadline arrives two days after the game.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars rout Colts, lead the South by three

stories.text: Jaguars blow out Colts 42-7 and lead the South by three games
stories.summary: Jacksonville scored the first 35 points at EverBank Stadium and moved to 5-2, three games clear of idle Houston. Trevor Lawrence went 10 of 14 for 210 yards and three touchdowns before leaving early in the fourth quarter. Rayuan Lane III returned an interception 92 yards for a score just before halftime.

stories.text: Hamilton and Murray are done for the season
stories.summary: Coach Liam Coen said nose tackle DaVon Hamilton (quad) and safety Eric Murray (elbow) will miss the rest of the year. Defensive end Travon Walker (ribs) and running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle and foot) did not practice Monday. Safety Antonio Johnson was limited with an ankle injury, and Coen said only that they would see on his Thursday status.

stories.text: Tuten runs for 104 and adds a receiving score
stories.summary: Bhayshul Tuten carried 16 times for 104 yards, including a 39-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. He caught a 25-yard screen pass for another score on the last play of the third quarter. Chris Rodriguez Jr. added 41 yards and a 28-yard touchdown run.

stories.text: 183: Jaguars rushing yards, a season high
stories.summary: Jacksonville ran 33 times for 183 yards and two touchdowns against Indianapolis. It was the team's best rushing day of the season. Lawrence needed only 14 pass attempts.

stories.text: Jaguars face Ravens on a short week
stories.summary: Jacksonville plays at Baltimore on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video at M&T Bank Stadium. It is the Jaguars' only Thursday night game this season. The Ravens are 4-4, and Jacksonville has to replace two season-ending injuries on defense in three days.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans trade Simmons, then lose in overtime

stories.text: Titans send Jeffery Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks
stories.summary: Tennessee traded the 29-year-old tackle and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Bears for a 2027 first, a 2027 fourth and a 2028 first. Simmons signed an extension in June that runs through 2030. It is the first time since 1967 that an interior lineman has brought back multiple first-rounders, per the report. The Titans were 1-6 when the deal came together.

stories.text: Line and secondary lose bodies in Cincinnati
stories.summary: Tennessee lost right tackle JC Latham (finger), left guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring, carted off), cornerback Marcus Harris (left ankle, carted off) and linebacker James Williams Sr. (groin) during the overtime loss. Rookie receiver Carnell Tate sat out with a shoulder injury. The next status update is expected Nov. 11, and the team is on its bye this week.

stories.text: Ward posts his first 300-yard game in a loss
stories.summary: Cam Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati. It was his first 300-yard game in 25 NFL starts. He also lost a fumble on a sack and took a 13-yard sack late in regulation that hurt a game-winning field goal try.

stories.text: 5: Amani Hooker leads the NFL in interceptions
stories.summary: Hooker picked off Joe Burrow three times Sunday, the first Titan with three in a game since Kevin Byard in 2017. He now has five interceptions this season. Coach Robert Saleh said Hooker is playing at a Pro Bowl level.

stories.text: Bye week, then Jacksonville comes to Nashville
stories.summary: Tennessee is on its bye in Week 9. The Titans return Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1:00 PM ET on Fox, hosting AFC South leader Jacksonville. The NFL trade deadline falls on Nov. 10, before that game.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos rally past KC and take the AFC West

stories.text: Broncos erase an 11-point deficit and grab first place in the AFC West
stories.summary: Denver outscored Kansas City 15-0 over the final two drives to win 28-24 on Sunday. Bo Nix hit Nate Adkins for a touchdown, and Jonah Coleman ran in the go-ahead score. The defense then stopped the Chiefs at the goal line on the last snap. The win is Denver's fourth straight, and it flipped the head-to-head tiebreaker.

stories.text: Safety Brandon Jones leaves with a hamstring injury
stories.summary: Starting safety Brandon Jones went down with a hamstring injury against Kansas City after three tackles, and no return timeline has come out. JL Skinner took his snaps and made the tackle at the 1-yard line on the Chiefs' last drive. Running back RJ Harvey went on injured reserve before the game, which opened the lead role for Coleman.

stories.text: Bo Nix stays clean and keeps winning late
stories.summary: Nix finished 20 of 32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns, a 103.9 passer rating that is his best of the season. At least five of his throws got batted at the line, and Sean Payton split the blame between Kansas City's rush and Denver's protection. Nix has now thrown 164 straight passes without an interception, the sixth-longest streak in Broncos history.

stories.text: 12: fourth-quarter comebacks for Nix since 2024
stories.summary: Nix now has 15 game-winning drives and 12 fourth-quarter comebacks since he entered the league in 2024. Both totals tie the most by any quarterback in his first three seasons, and both lead the NFL over that span. Sunday added another one against the team Denver is chasing in the division.

stories.text: Broncos visit Carolina before the bye
stories.summary: Denver plays at the Panthers (3-4) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. A win would make five straight for the Broncos. They then get their Week 10 bye, so watch how the secondary holds up without Jones.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs lose a lead and a kicking debate

stories.text: Chiefs blow an 11-point lead as Butker misses from 54
stories.summary: Kansas City went scoreless in the fourth quarter and lost 28-24 in Denver, its second straight defeat. Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal wide right with 2:36 left, and Jonah Coleman scored for Denver two plays later. On the final snap, a false start on Jaylon Moore erased a Rashee Rice touchdown, and Patrick Mahomes was sacked to end it. Andy Reid said the kick was within Butker's range.

stories.text: Simmons stays on IR, Thornton's ankle still a question
stories.summary: Tackle Josh Simmons went on injured reserve about a week ago. Receiver Tyquan Thornton has an ankle injury with no update from the team, and his absence has hurt the deep passing game. Rice (hamstring) and Moore (concussion protocol) were both practicing before the Denver game, and both played Sunday. The most recent injury details come from Reid's Oct. 28 press conference.

stories.text: Mahomes throws for 321 and still loses
stories.summary: Mahomes went 30 of 41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He is in his first season back from reconstructive knee surgery. He took two sacks, including the one that ended the game, and said afterward the team's execution was not at a high enough level.

stories.text: 11 penalties for 105 yards: a season high for Kansas City
stories.summary: The Chiefs set a season high with 11 penalties for 105 yards in Denver, and Reid called the flags a major concern. Denver pressured Mahomes on the decisive drives, and Kansas City managed no points in the final 15 minutes. Butker has missed 16 kicks since the start of last season, the most in the league over that stretch.

stories.text: Jets visit Arrowhead with a kicker decision looming
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts the Jets (2-6) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Justin Tucker, signed to the practice squad last week, made all 30 of his tryout kicks, so watch whether Reid sticks with Butker. The trade deadline is Nov. 10.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders end four-game skid with 38-33 win

stories.text: Raiders rally from nine down to beat the Jets and snap a four-game slide
stories.summary: Las Vegas trailed by nine at the half and won 38-33 at MetLife Stadium. Kirk Cousins put the Raiders ahead with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Nailor with 11:33 left. Jeremy Chinn intercepted Geno Smith in the end zone on the final play to seal it. The win moves Las Vegas back to 4-4.

stories.text: Cornerback Darien Porter hurts his groin on the first defensive snap
stories.summary: Cornerback Darien Porter injured his groin on the Raiders' first defensive play against the Jets and did not return. No status update has come out yet. Geno Smith went on to throw for 290 yards against the Raiders' secondary, so watch the injury report this week ahead of the trip to San Francisco.

stories.text: Brock Bowers passes Mike Ditka in the record book
stories.summary: Bowers caught seven passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets. His 2,386 receiving yards are the most by a non-wide receiver through his first 35 NFL games, passing Mike Ditka. He opened the scoring with a 12-yard touchdown from Cousins on the first drive.

stories.text: 19 of 26: Cousins's day, plus a rushing score
stories.summary: Cousins finished 19 of 26 for 247 yards and three touchdown passes with no interceptions, and he added a 1-yard sneak for his first rushing touchdown of the year. Las Vegas scored on six of its nine full possessions. Dylan Laube also returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown.

stories.text: Raiders head to Santa Clara for a late-afternoon test
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at the 49ers (6-1) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 PM ET on Fox at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco lost its first game of the year last week, a 29-20 defeat in Atlanta in which it turned the ball over four times. Watch whether the Raiders can protect their takeaway edge and slow a 49ers rushing attack that may see Christian McCaffrey limited by a mild hamstring strain.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers fall to the Rams 24-9

stories.text: Chargers drop to 0-7 and are the NFL's only winless team
stories.summary: The Rams scored 21 unanswered points in the second half and beat Los Angeles 24-9 on Sunday. The Chargers never reached the end zone and settled for three field goals. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 157 yards, but Blake Corum's 23-yard run and Puka Nacua's screen score broke it open. The Chargers have lost seven straight.

stories.text: Njoku likely to open his practice window
stories.summary: Jim Harbaugh said Monday that tight end David Njoku, on injured reserve since a Week 2 knee injury, will likely have his 21-day practice window opened this week. Guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) should return to practice after missing five games. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley (hamstrings) are ramping up, and Deane Leonard remains in concussion protocol.

stories.text: Herbert throws for 257 but gives it away twice
stories.summary: Justin Herbert went 24 of 32 for 257 yards against the Rams, with interceptions to Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie. The McDuffie pick led to a Los Angeles touchdown. Herbert has thrown an interception in every game this season and leads the league with 10. Ladd McConkey led the receivers with four catches for 86 yards.

stories.text: 9: straight quarters without a Chargers touchdown
stories.summary: Los Angeles has not scored a touchdown since the third quarter of Week 5, a span of nine straight quarters. Four drives against the Rams started at or past the Rams' 40-yard line, and they produced three points. A last-second Hail Mary before halftime fell about three feet short.

stories.text: Texans come to town with win No. 1 in play
stories.summary: The Chargers host the Texans on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. Harbaugh said he is focused on Houston and not the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Watch the turnovers first, since Herbert's interceptions have stalled the offense all year.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys cough up 14-point lead, fall in OT

stories.text: Cowboys blow a 14-point lead and lose to Arizona in overtime
stories.summary: Dallas led Arizona 24-10 with 14:20 left in the fourth quarter and lost 33-30 when Chad Ryland hit a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Owner Jerry Jones said afterward that a midseason coaching change is not on his mind, and he called the failure team-wide. Brian Schottenheimer, now 10-13-1 in his second year, took the blame.

stories.text: Two rookie defensive starters are hurt, and Downs is in the concussion protocol
stories.summary: Safety Caleb Downs is in the concussion protocol and his status for Indianapolis is in doubt. Linebacker Malachi Lawrence, who just moved into the starting lineup, hurt something that Schottenheimer said is worse than first thought and could cost him multiple weeks. Tight end Jake Ferguson rolled an ankle but has a chance to play, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is waiting on test results.

stories.text: Caleb Downs leads Dallas in tackles as a rookie
stories.summary: Downs has 52 tackles, 30 of them solo, plus a sack, two forced fumbles and a pass defensed through eight games. He leads the Cowboys in tackles while moving between nickel, run support and deeper alignments. He left the Arizona game in the fourth quarter after tackling Tyler Allgeier on a touchdown, so the Cowboys may lose their most versatile defender this week.

stories.text: 27: second-half points Arizona scored on the Cowboys
stories.summary: Arizona outgained Dallas 286-157 after halftime and scored 27 of its 33 points over the last two quarters and overtime. The Cardinals went 4 for 5 on third down and 3 for 3 in the red zone in the second half. Schottenheimer said his team failed to finish in all three phases.

stories.text: Cowboys visit the 2-6 Colts on Sunday
stories.summary: Dallas plays at Indianapolis on Sunday, November 8 at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. The Colts have lost four straight, including a 42-7 loss at Jacksonville, and have given the ball away 15 times in eight games. Watch the Dallas secondary, which may be without Downs and could be thin elsewhere.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Rested Giants lead the East at the bye's end

stories.text: Giants hold the NFC East lead after the bye with three quarterbacks used
stories.summary: New York is 4-2-1 and guaranteed to stay in first place when play resumes, with a two-game lead in the win column. The Giants are the first team since 1950 to win with three different quarterbacks in its first seven games, and J.J. McCarthy has taken the job after Jaxson Dart's knee injury. General manager Joe Schoen said the front office would use the bye to weigh trade options before the November 10 deadline.

stories.text: Tracy goes on injured reserve with a hamstring injury
stories.summary: Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. suffered the hamstring injury against Houston and will miss at least four games, with a possible return in Week 13 against San Francisco. Schoen said the injury should not be long-term. Cam Skattebo is listed day to day, and edge rusher Abdul Carter missed a practice with an illness.

stories.text: Skattebo runs for a career-high 124 yards in Houston
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo got 17 carries against the Texans after receiving no touches the week before, and he ran for a career-best 124 yards. He scored from 16 yards to put New York up 21-14 and broke a 42-yard run in overtime. Devin Singletary finished the 27-21 win with a 30-yard touchdown run.

stories.text: 15-3: John Harbaugh's record in games right after a bye
stories.summary: Harbaugh has won 15 of 18 games coming off a bye week. The Giants resume play at Philadelphia, then host Washington on a Thursday night five days later. Both opponents sit below New York in the NFC East.

stories.text: Giants open the second half at Philadelphia
stories.summary: New York plays at the 2-6 Eagles on Sunday, November 8 at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. Philadelphia has lost six straight and will start Tanner McKee while Jalen Hurts stays out. The Giants then host Washington on Thursday, November 12 at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles drop sixth straight, face a deadline test

stories.text: Eagles lose their sixth straight and face a trade deadline decision
stories.summary: Philadelphia led Washington 10-0 and lost 27-10 on Sunday night, its sixth straight loss and the first such skid since 2012. The deadline is November 10. ESPN reported that Saquon Barkley will not be traded, but general manager Howie Roseman could still move veterans on expiring or longer deals.

stories.text: Hurts remains out with blood clots while Barkley plays hurt
stories.summary: Quarterback Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve with a deep vein thrombosis and clots in both lungs. He is on blood thinners and cannot take part in contact football. Barkley played through hamstring and back problems on a pitch count against Washington, and cornerback Michael Carter II re-injured his abdomen and did not return.

stories.text: McKee throws for 212 yards in a losing effort
stories.summary: Tanner McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, and he ran four times for 25 yards. Makai Lemon caught six passes for 57 yards and Eli Stowers added three for 53. The defense did its part with sacks from Jalen Carter and Nolan Smith Jr., but the offense stalled after the early lead.

stories.text: 6: straight losses, the Eagles' longest skid since 2012
stories.summary: Philadelphia sits last in the NFC East at 2-6. The Eagles have scored 137 points and allowed 202 this season, a deficit of 65. They are averaging 265.3 yards per game, and their playoff odds are slim.

stories.text: Eagles host the Giants, then take their bye
stories.summary: Philadelphia faces New York at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, November 8 at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. The Eagles are home underdogs. They are off in Week 10, then host Pittsburgh on November 22.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Daniels rallies Commanders past Eagles

stories.text: Daniels rallies Washington from a 10-0 hole to beat Philadelphia
stories.summary: Washington scored 27 straight points to beat the Eagles 27-10 on Sunday night. Jayden Daniels called the offense together on the sideline after a start that included four penalties, a missed 55-yard field goal and a fumble. It was his first win since October 5, 2025, ending an 0-7-1 run in his previous eight starts, and it puts Washington two games behind first-place New York.

stories.text: Running back McNichols leaves with a foot injury
stories.summary: Jeremy McNichols left the Eagles game after five carries for 21 yards, and the team fears the foot injury could be significant. He is getting more tests, and Washington awaits results. He had only just come back from injured reserve after missing the first five weeks with a quad problem, and Terry McLaurin remains out for the season.

stories.text: Daniels throws for 217 yards, takes care of the ball
stories.summary: Daniels went 16 of 29 for 217 yards and a touchdown, and ran for 23 more. He went 5 of 8 for 121 yards in the second half after getting the wind knocked out of him late in the first. He has six touchdown passes and no interceptions on the season.

stories.text: 46.5%: Washington's pressure rate, a season high
stories.summary: The defense pressured Philadelphia on 46.5 percent of dropbacks, its highest mark of the year according to NFL+, and recorded five sacks. One sack set up a fumble recovery deep in Eagles territory, and Washington has now taken the ball away in five straight games. Rasul Douglas sealed the win with a fourth-down interception.

stories.text: Commanders host the Rams on Sunday
stories.summary: Washington plays Los Angeles at Northwest Stadium on Sunday, November 8 at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. The Rams are 4-4 and have won back-to-back games over the Chargers and Raiders. Washington then visits the Giants on Thursday, November 12 at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Simmons debuts, Bears rout the champs

stories.text: Simmons makes his debut and the Bears bury Seattle 34-17
stories.summary: Jeffery Simmons played his first game for Chicago four days after the trade with Tennessee. He finished with six tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss as the Bears beat the defending champion Seahawks on Monday night. Chicago improved to 6-2 and has won three straight.

stories.text: Muhammad sits out with a toe injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Malik Muhammad missed the Seattle game with a toe problem he picked up in the Week 7 win over New England. He logged three limited practices during the week and still could not go. Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips handled the outside corner snaps.

stories.text: Swift grinds out three second-half touchdowns
stories.summary: D'Andre Swift carried 27 times for 69 yards against Seattle. He found the end zone on runs of 1, 5 and 5 yards, all after halftime, as Chicago pulled away from a 13-9 lead at the break.

stories.text: 1-for-11: Seattle's third-down mark against Chicago
stories.summary: The Seahawks converted one of 11 third downs and punted away five three-and-outs. Chicago gained 363 yards to Seattle's 252. Jaxon Smith-Njigba still caught six passes for 118 yards and a score.

stories.text: Bucs visit Soldier Field on Sunday night
stories.summary: Chicago hosts Tampa Bay on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Bears will watch to see if Simmons and Montez Sweat keep the pressure up on a second straight week.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions hand Vikings their first loss

stories.text: Lions stop the unbeaten Vikings 19-15 at Ford Field
stories.summary: Jared Goff hit Jameson Williams for a 7-yard touchdown with 4:35 left to put Detroit ahead for good. Minnesota had led 15-12 in the fourth quarter. The win moved Detroit to 5-2 and dropped the Vikings to 6-1.

stories.text: Linebacker Jack Campbell in hospital with a neck injury
stories.summary: Campbell went down on the first play of the fourth quarter and left the field on a backboard. The Lions said Monday that he continues to rest in the hospital and that early indications are positive. Brian Branch and DJ Wonnum both suffered concussions in the first half, so the defense heads into Miami thin.

stories.text: Gibbs runs for 153 and a tackle-breaking touchdown
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the Detroit offense against Minnesota. He ran for 153 yards, including a 30-yard touchdown in the third quarter where he shook off several tacklers.

stories.text: 230: rushing yards for Detroit against Minnesota
stories.summary: The Lions ran for 230 yards, and 164 of them came in the second half. Goff threw for only 176 yards on 18-of-25 passing. The ground game wore down a Vikings defense that gave up 13 points after halftime.

stories.text: Lions travel to Miami for a Sunday afternoon game
stories.summary: Detroit plays at the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The league moved the game from Fox to CBS. Watch the injury report for Campbell, Branch and Wonnum.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Love throws three TDs in Thursday win

stories.text: Packers hold off Carolina 27-19 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes as Green Bay moved to 5-3. The Packers led 27-10 in the third quarter, then watched Carolina outgain them 109-32 in the fourth. Green Bay still sits behind the other three NFC North teams on record.

stories.text: Watson cleared after hospital trip, Whyle in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Christian Watson went to a hospital for chest testing in the first half, got a clean result and returned to finish with 113 yards. Tight end Josh Whyle suffered a concussion and was ruled out.

stories.text: Love picks apart the Panthers blitz
stories.summary: Love finished 30-of-41 for 288 yards and three touchdowns. He started 9-for-9 against the blitz and ended 14-of-16 for 126 yards and two scores when Carolina sent extra rushers. He did throw one interception, on a deep ball intended for Matthew Golden.

stories.text: 6: sacks by the Packers defense on Bryce Young
stories.summary: Green Bay sacked Young six times, with Ty'Ron Hopper and Lukas Van Ness among those getting home. Rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton added a sack and combined with Van Ness on another. Hopper also intercepted a pass.

stories.text: Packers head to Foxborough to face the Patriots
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at New England on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Both teams are 5-3. The Patriots plan to honor the 10th anniversary of their Super Bowl LI win.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten run ends as offense stalls

stories.text: Vikings fall 19-15 in Detroit and lose for the first time
stories.summary: Minnesota dropped to 6-1 and 2-1 in the division. The offense ran for 81 yards, converted 3 of 10 third downs and missed a 57-yard field goal. Kyler Murray called the loss on his own mistakes and said the team was not good enough.

stories.text: Murray evaluated for a hamstring issue before Buffalo
stories.summary: Murray felt hamstring tightness late in the Detroit game and went to the medical tent after his touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson. He returned for the next drive. Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Murray was sore and the team was running a full evaluation. Safety Theo Jackson also hurt his quad.

stories.text: Murray throws two touchdowns in a loss
stories.summary: Murray went 17-of-29 for 210 yards with touchdown passes to Justin Jefferson and Hockenson, plus one interception. He took three sacks. Minnesota had led 15-12 in the fourth quarter before Detroit drove for the winning score.

stories.text: 32nd: where Minnesota ranks in first downs per game
stories.summary: Through seven games the Vikings rank last in the league in first downs per game and 31st in offensive touchdowns per game. They are 29th in yards per game and 27th in points.

stories.text: Bills come to Minneapolis on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Buffalo on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Murray's hamstring is the question to watch.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Penix's four picks sink Falcons in the rain

stories.text: Penix throws four picks as Falcons get shut out in Tampa
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. went 8 of 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions in a 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers, the worst game of his career by his own account. Atlanta fell to 3-5 and passed up a chance to take the NFC South lead. Kevin Stefanski said he has no concerns about Penix going forward, and Penix promised a bounce-back after throwing one interception in his first six starts.

stories.text: Ebukam and Branch ruled out for Bengals game in Madrid
stories.summary: Stefanski ruled out edge rusher Samson Ebukam and receiver Zachariah Branch for Week 9, both with hamstring injuries. The defense does get James Pearce Jr. back, since he has finished his eight-game suspension and can play against Cincinnati.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson leads the league even in a lost day
stories.summary: Robinson ran 19 times for 76 yards in the rain and still sits first in the NFL with 780 rushing yards. Tampa Bay's backs out-carried him, and critics of the game plan say Atlanta leaned on Penix's arm when the ground game was its better option.

stories.text: 0-for-12: Falcons never moved the chains on third down
stories.summary: Atlanta failed on all 12 third-down tries against Tampa Bay, its worst third-down day of the year. The Falcons now convert 33.3 percent of the time this season, which ranks 29th in the league. They also ran 28 times for 99 yards while the Bucs piled up 324 on the ground.

stories.text: Falcons head to Madrid to face the Bengals Sunday
stories.summary: Atlanta plays Cincinnati at Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. Watch whether Pearce can add juice to the pass rush and whether the offense finds a third-down answer.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Young sacked six times in Thursday loss

stories.text: Panthers fall to Packers 27-19 as Young takes six sacks
stories.summary: Carolina trailed 27-10 in the third quarter and outgained Green Bay 109 to 32 in the fourth, but it never closed the gap. Bryce Young finished 23 of 41 for 209 yards, a touchdown and an interception, and an incompletion on fourth-and-5 with 2:41 left ended the last real threat. The Panthers sit at 3-4, and coach Dave Canales said Young's knee may be limiting his mobility.

stories.text: Secondary thins out as Will Lee leaves with hamstring injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Will Lee went to the locker room in a cart with a hamstring injury, and guard Corey Bullock left with a quad issue in the second half. Carolina already has cornerbacks Jaycee Horn, Akayleb Evans and Mike Jackson on injured reserve, so the depth chart is running short.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard carries the load in the loss
stories.summary: Hubbard ran 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown and added seven catches for 38 yards, touching the ball 29 times. Receiver Tetairoa McMillan chipped in six catches for 58 yards.

stories.text: 6: sacks Green Bay put on Bryce Young Thursday night
stories.summary: The Packers sacked Young six times and hit him nine times. Carolina forced three turnovers in the game and turned them into only a field goal, which left the pressure as the difference.

stories.text: Panthers host Denver at 1 p.m. ET Sunday on CBS
stories.summary: Carolina plays the Broncos at home on Sunday, Nov. 8, with a 1 p.m. ET kickoff, and CBS has the broadcast. Watch Young's protection and the status of the banged-up secondary against Denver.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints fire run-game coach after bye-week review

stories.text: Saints fire run-game coordinator after 18-yard day in Paris
stories.summary: New Orleans fired run-game coordinator T.J. Paganetti during the bye week, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The Saints gained 18 rushing yards on 17 carries in the 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh, their worst ground game since 1999. It is the first major staff move Kellen Moore has made, and the team sits last in the NFC South at 2-5.

stories.text: Donaldson, Reid and Ruiz carry questions into the Browns game
stories.summary: Running back CJ Donaldson left the Paris game with a shoulder injury, and safety Justin Reid is coming back from an apparent concussion. Guard Cesar Ruiz returned to practice from a knee injury but did not start, with rookie Jeremiah Wright taking his spot.

stories.text: Tyler Shough was sharp in Paris, and the run game wasted it
stories.summary: Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards and a touchdown against the Steelers. Rookie receiver Barion Brown supplied the longest play, a 49-yard catch. The passing game was not the issue in the loss.

stories.text: 18: rushing yards the Saints managed on 17 carries
stories.summary: That was New Orleans' lowest rushing total since an 11-yard game in 1999. The defense has also allowed at least 100 net rushing yards in every game but one, so the trouble runs both directions.

stories.text: Saints return from bye to host Browns Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: New Orleans hosts Cleveland at the Superdome on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Saints are 0-3 at home this season, and the Browns are a road team looking for a win.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs win 16-0 without a completed pass

stories.text: Bucs beat Falcons 16-0 without completing a pass
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield went 0 for 3 in the rain, and Tampa Bay still won by running for a franchise-record 324 yards. No team had won a game without a completion since the 1974 Bills. The Bucs are 3-5 and 2-0 in the NFC South.

stories.text: Egbuka sits out with foot injury, Week 9 return not confirmed
stories.summary: Receiver Emeka Egbuka missed the Falcons game with a foot injury. A report from the Bucs' site on Oct. 30 pointed to the Bears game as his next possible return, but the team had not confirmed that. Mayfield is two games back from a right thumb injury.

stories.text: Alex Anzalone intercepts Penix twice in first quarter
stories.summary: The linebacker had two interceptions, six tackles, a tackle for loss and two passes defensed. Both picks came in Atlanta territory, and Penix had thrown only one interception all year before Sunday.

stories.text: 324: franchise-record rushing yards for Tampa Bay
stories.summary: Bucky Irving ran 27 times for 170 yards and Kenny Gainwell 25 times for 140, the first teammates in NFL history with 25 carries and 125 yards each in the same game. The old team record was 283 yards from 2015. The Bucs ran on 92 percent of their plays.

stories.text: Bucs visit Bears on Sunday Night Football, then bye
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at Soldier Field on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Chicago allows 87.6 rushing yards per game, fourth fewest in the league before Monday night, which tests the Bucs' run-heavy approach. The Bucs have a bye in Week 10.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Minshew gets the nod after Dallas rally

stories.text: Cardinals turn to Minshew at quarterback for Seattle
stories.summary: Mike LaFleur pulled Jacoby Brissett in Dallas and watched Gardner Minshew II lead four straight touchdown drives to force overtime in a 33-30 win. Minshew went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns with no turnovers, including a 13-yard strike to Michael Wilson with six seconds left in regulation. LaFleur held off naming a starter on Sunday night, then Arizona confirmed Minshew on Monday.

stories.text: Love hurts the other ankle, Knight in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Rookie back Jeremiyah Love rolled his right ankle against Dallas after already missing time with a left ankle problem. LaFleur called it a new injury and promised an update later this week. Bam Knight entered the concussion protocol, which leaves Tyler Allgeier as the only healthy back. Receiver Kendrick Bourne (ankle) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee) also left the game.

stories.text: Allgeier carries the backfield on a bad toe
stories.summary: Tyler Allgeier piled up a career-high 191 scrimmage yards and scored twice while playing through a toe injury. Next Gen Stats credited him with 96 rushing yards over expected, the most by an Arizona runner since 2018. He now stands as the lone healthy back heading into Seattle.

stories.text: 14: points Arizona erased to stun Dallas
stories.summary: Dallas led 17-3 late in the third quarter, and Arizona scored on four straight possessions to finish regulation, then won in overtime. The defense helped by holding the Cowboys to 3.6 yards per play and 2.4 per carry, with four sacks. Minshew also went 3 for 3 in the red zone, where the offense had been stuck.

stories.text: At Seattle on Sunday with a new starter
stories.summary: Arizona (3-5) visits the Seahawks (4-4) on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch whether Minshew keeps the red zone gains going behind a banged-up line and a thin backfield. Arizona hosts the Rams the following week.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Ground game and defense carry second straight win

stories.text: Rams run past winless Chargers for a second straight win
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat the Chargers 24-9 at SoFi Stadium to reach 4-4. The offense had no first downs through three first-half possessions, then Blake Corum and Kyren Williams took over after halftime. Corum ran for 73 yards and a 23-yard score to open the third quarter, and Williams added a touchdown. Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie each intercepted a pass, and those takeaways set up 10 points.

stories.text: Garrett's clock starts, cornerbacks day to day
stories.summary: Sean McVay said Myles Garrett (knee) will practice this week, which opens his 21-day window off injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is more likely than not to start his own window. Cornerback Jaylen Watson aggravated his shoulder and is day to day, McDuffie is being monitored for a back issue, and linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring) is week to week.

stories.text: Nacua is the offense's lone reliable target
stories.summary: Puka Nacua caught 11 of his 12 targets for 80 yards and finished with an 18-yard screen touchdown from Matthew Stafford that made it 24-9. The other receivers combined for two catches on six targets. Wide receiver depth behind Nacua remains the offense's clearest weakness.

stories.text: 119: rushing yards by two backs after halftime
stories.summary: Corum and Williams managed 10 yards on five carries in the first half. After the break they ran 22 times for 119 yards. The Rams posted the third-best rushing efficiency in the league in Week 8, at 0.15 EPA per rush.

stories.text: At Washington on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: The Rams (4-4) visit the Commanders (2-4-1) on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch Stafford's quick release against a Washington line that sacked Philadelphia five times, and whether Garrett or Watson are cleared by the end of the week. Los Angeles then plays at Arizona in Week 10.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Bye ends with a stack of key returns in view

stories.text: Niners come off the bye hoping to get healthy at receiver
stories.summary: San Francisco sits at 6-1 after its first loss, a 29-20 defeat at Atlanta, and now hosts Las Vegas. The big question is how many injured players come back. Nick Bosa, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel all have a chance to return, and Kyle Shanahan said Evans needs no more testing. Not everyone is guaranteed to play on Nov. 8.

stories.text: Bosa, Evans, Samuel and Robinson eye a return
stories.summary: Bosa has been out since a calf strain before Week 3, and there is plenty of optimism he returns now. Samuel has missed two games with a hamstring injury, while Evans sat out after playing through rib and Achilles problems. Demarcus Robinson (high ankle sprain) is eligible off injured reserve. Christian McCaffrey had a mild hamstring strain against Atlanta. Final designations come later this week.

stories.text: Purdy sits at 15 touchdowns and four picks
stories.summary: Brock Purdy has thrown 15 touchdowns against four interceptions through seven games, and he has done it with a thinned-out receiver room. The Atlanta game was his only real stumble. The offense ranks first in success rate and first in defense-adjusted value over average, per The San Francisco Standard.

stories.text: 52.7%: San Francisco's offensive success rate leads the NFL
stories.summary: No offense in the league wins more plays than the Niners' unit. The rushing success rate has climbed above 50 percent, up from 41.8 percent in 2025. The line ranks first in ESPN's pass block win rate, though left guard Connor Colby has allowed 20 pressures.

stories.text: Raiders visit Levi's on Sunday
stories.summary: San Francisco (6-1) hosts Las Vegas (4-4) on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. The Raiders just beat the Jets 38-33 and rank 27th in defensive DVOA, so the offense should find room if the receivers return. The Niners then travel to Dallas in Week 10.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Bears rout exposes sloppy Seahawks in all three phases

stories.text: Seahawks take their worst loss under Macdonald
stories.summary: Chicago won 34-17 on Monday night, and Mike Macdonald said his team lost in all three phases. Seattle's special teams gave away a missed extra point, a blocked field goal, two 15-yard penalties and a misplayed punt that became a touchback. The Seahawks drop to 4-4.

stories.text: Williams exits with a stinger, backs return
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Leonard Williams left late in the third quarter with a stinger, and Macdonald said they would see how it shakes out. Outside linebacker Connor O'Toole left with a foot injury. On the positive side, Jadarian Price came off injured reserve after a four-game chest injury absence, and Zach Charbonnet played for the first time since tearing his ACL in January. Both said they came out fine.

stories.text: Smith-Njigba keeps producing in a loss
stories.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught six passes for 118 yards and a 43-yard touchdown against Chicago. It was his seventh 100-yard game in eight outings. He leads the league with 985 receiving yards.

stories.text: 1 for 11: Seattle's third-down night against Chicago
stories.summary: The offense converted one third down in 11 tries and punted five times. Sam Darnold finished 17 of 34 for 188 yards and was sacked three times. Chicago, meanwhile, went 7 for 15 on third down and 4 for 4 in the red zone.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Lumen Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Seattle (4-4) hosts Arizona (3-5) on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch whether the Seahawks clean up special teams and how Leonard Williams' stinger develops. Seattle visits Las Vegas in Week 10.
